observations: body L1-L2: the end of the sentence begun on p. 325. The title of appendix F (p. 149, L5-L9 of the translation) calls the right ascensions «ǵuwīrāst Capricorni» and the oblique ones «ǵuwīrāst regionis».

body L3-L4: «26–27» has a long dash (5.4 pt); the ellipses have five dots each. The places are p. 149, L21 («eamque de residuorum differentia deme; quod remanet») and L26-L27 («eam de residuorum differentia deme; quod remanet») by the count of that page; Nallino's addenda (Part I, p. LXXII) point to this correction, as recorded on p. 149.

body L5-L17: «al–Ḥaṣṣār», «Ibn al–Bannā’», «al–Qalaṣādī» (L7, L14) and «Woepcke» are letter-spaced; the dashes of «al–Ḥaṣṣār», «al–Bannā’», «al–Qalaṣādī» and «al–musammà» measure 5.2, 5.2, 5.4 and 5.4 pt, the dash before «Idem» 10.0 pt. The examples are right: 2/5 + 1/3 · 1/5 = 7/15, and 5/11 + 4/11 · 1/7 + 1/11 · 1/7 · 1/5 = (175 + 20 + 1)/385 = 196/385. In the notations of L11 each numerator stands over its own denominator, 2 over 5 and 1 over 3, 5 over 11, 4 over 7 and 1 over 5, as set; the bar of the first prints only in part. The o of «denominator» (L12) did not print. The Arabic of L15 is set as printed, with the shadda of اقلّ and the vowel signs of فسَمِّها. A mark like an apostrophe stands at the right edge after «[in» (L15), and a speck below the line after «al–Qalaṣādī,» (L14); they are not transcribed. Nallino's addenda (Part I, pp. LXXIX-LXXX, «326»): among the eastern Arabs the verb «denominare» seems to be used only of fractions: so in ‘Omar al-Khayyāmī's Algebra (ed. Woepcke, Paris 1851), p. 42, l. 6 and 8 of the text, the part of a number is the part named after that number, as the third after three, and the part of the square the part named after its number (p. 69 of the translation); in John of Seville's Liber algorismi de pratica arismetrice (Boncompagni, Trattati d'aritmetica, Rome 1857, fasc. II), p. 49, the Indians chose to make the «denominatio» of their fractions from sixty, with further examples on pp. 55-70; on nisbah in the sense of tasmiyah, pp. 326-27. Likewise in Hebrew, in Abraham bar Ḥiyya's arithmetic (first half of the twelfth century) the chapter on dividing a number by a number is distinguished from the chapter on knowing the ratio of a number to a number, that is, on dividing the smaller by the larger (Steinschneider, Abraham ibn Esra, Abhandlungen zur Geschichte der Mathematik III, 1880, p. 108, did not understand the word); Abraham ibn Ezra uses ‘ērek, ratio, in the same sense (ibid. p. 101, note 157, and p. 108, note 184, where Steinschneider wrongly renders it «Proportion»).

body L18-L22: «semidiur-» has a hyphen (2.5 pt). The factor distantia : arcus semidiurnus equals horae temporales distantiae : 6 because the semidiurnal arc is six temporal hours, so that the proportional part is the term (β − α) × horae temporales distantiae : 6 of the rule (α) on p. 316, the difference of the residues being that of the oblique and the right ascensions. The bar of the second fraction of L21 prints in pieces, and the 6 stands left of its middle.

body L23-L24: the places are p. 149, L31 («compara arcui seminocturno (2), et secundum hanc proportionem sume quantitatem») and L36 («compara dimidio (3) arcui diurno, et hac ratione quantitatem sume») by the count of that page. The hyphen of «com-» measures 2.5 pt. The sentence continues on p. 327.

notes_left L1-L7: «Ibn al–Hā’im» and «Ahlwardt» are letter-spaced; the dash of «al–Hā’im» measures 4.3 pt and is set as a long dash, the hyphen of «al-ma‘ūnah» 3.4 pt, the dash before «Vocem» 7.1 pt. «occur» (L5) is printed without the hyphen of its division. The month sha‘bān 791 ran from 25 July to 22 August 1389 (tabular calendar, astronomical epoch). A speck in the margin before «typis» (L3) is not transcribed.

notes_left L8-L13: «Suter» and «el-Ḥaṣṣàr» are letter-spaced; the title of Suter's article is set as printed, with the grave accents of «Abù Zakarijà» and «Ḥaṣṣàr»; «el-Ḥaṣṣàr» has a hyphen (3.2 pt), «12-40» and «17-20» hyphens (3.4 pt each).

notes_left L14-L18: «Suter», «Marre» and «Ibn Albannâ» are letter-spaced. The year 740 of the hijrah began on 8 July 1339 (tabular calendar, astronomical epoch), as printed. «162-64» has a hyphen (3.7 pt); its 2 prints broken.
notes_right L1-L2: the end of note 3; «1863-64» and «289-319» have hyphens (3.4 pt each).

notes_right L3-L12: «Suter», «Woepcke» and «Al-» «kalçàdì» are letter-spaced; the hyphen of «Al-» (1.9 pt) divides the name. The month dhū ’l-ḥiǵǵah 891 ran from 27 November to 26 December 1486 (tabular calendar, astronomical epoch), at the end of 1486, as printed. A speck before «dhū» (L3) is not transcribed. «’l-ḥiǵǵah» and «al-asrār» have hyphens (2.8 and 3.0 pt), as have «180-82», «1858-59», «230-275», «399-438» and «20-21»; the dash of «17–18» measures 4.3 pt and is set as a long dash.
notes_right L13-L18: «Hankel» and «Cantor» are letter-spaced; «370-71» and «764-65» have hyphens (3.1 and 3.6 pt).
